text:
maya: ran a quick nsys of a busy inference node, KV-prefetch looks serialized and we get long CPU gaps between memcpy+kernel bursts. attaching timeline screenshot: https://redwood.internal/attachments/1827654321/trace.png
chris: can you paste the timeline snippet/text? curious about stream IDs and memcpy streams vs compute streams
maya: snippet below (nsys timeline view):
```
[Stream 3] memcpy HtoD 0.8ms -> then 3ms idle -> [Stream 1] kernel small 1.2ms -> [Stream 3] memcpy HtoD 0.7ms -> kernel 1.0ms
CPU: prefetch_worker sleep 12ms -> wake -> memcpy submit -> blocked by scheduling 8ms
```
devon: looks like host prefetch thread is getting preempted by Linux scheduler which staggers memcpy submits; that would serialize the effective prefetch and make batching heuristics see sparse sequences
chris: did you capture OS runtime events in nsys? we want thread wake/sleep markers to confirm preemption spikes
maya: yes I included osrt trace. saw frequent "thread deschedule" on the prefetch worker around GC times and during background logging spikes
taylor: nice find. quick repro: try running prefetch worker pinned to an isolated core and SCHED_FIFO with chrt to see if memcpy/kernels overlap more consistently
devon: commands I used locally:
```bash
# pin and boost priority
taskset -c 24 chrt -f 99 ./kv_prefetch_worker --cpu-poll
# nsys capture
nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none ./inference_server
```
chris: also try perf sched record to get full scheduling timeline: `sudo perf record -e sched:sched_switch -a -o sched.data -- sleep 10` then `perf script -i sched.data`
maya: after pin+chrt we saw memcpy submissions cluster and kernel overlap increased, end-to-end latency p50 down ~7% p99 ~10% in the quick run
taylor: if that holds, we should adjust batcher heuristic to factor in host submit jitter + implement a hot-path for prefetch worker: pinned high-prio thread or offload to dedicated DMA engine if available
devon: another angle: reduce kernel launch stalls by using streams with less host-side dependency and enable async prefetch with CUDA streams and callbacks so submit doesn't rely on host thread scheduling
maya: good notes. next steps: (1) run longer 30min trace with osrt + cuda on prod replica (2) experiment with chrt/pinning + perf traces (3) try async prefetch branch and measure p99. I'll open a short PR with repro script and timeline links
sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026 prefetch-serialization-investigation, assigned to maya, priority P2
chris: thanks maya — please add the nsys capture command + minimal repro in the incident so others can reproduce quickly :thumbsup:
